title: Pass by address
recap: Pass by address passes a pointer value into a function. The function receives a copy of the address but can still modify the caller-owned object by indirection.
A nullable parameter can communicate optional participation. Document whether null is accepted and what it means instead of relying on accidental behavior.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement resetIfPresent(value). A non-null pointer means reset that caller-owned integer to zero. A null pointer means no action. Do not allocate, delete, or retain the address.
hints: Make null an early return or condition.
Only the pointee should be set to zero.
No ownership is transferred by this call.
